questions.question: With `box-sizing: content-box` (the default), what happens to an element's rendered width when you add padding?
options: Nothing — width always means the final rendered width
The element becomes visually wider than the specified width, since padding and border are added on top of it
The content shrinks to keep the total width the same
questions.explanation: content-box measures only the content area with `width`; padding and border are added on top, making the final rendered box larger than the declared width.

questions.question: Why do most modern CSS resets set `box-sizing: border-box` globally?
options: So that a declared width/height already includes padding and border, making fixed-width layouts behave predictably
It is required for Flexbox to work
questions.explanation: border-box means the box you set with width/height is the box you get, regardless of how much padding or border is added — far more predictable for layout work.

questions.question: What is the key difference between `inline` and `inline-block` display values?
options: inline-block respects width, height, and full margin like a block element while still flowing inline with surrounding content; inline ignores width/height and only applies horizontal margin
inline-block always takes up the full width of its container
inline elements cannot contain any text
questions.explanation: inline-block is the hybrid: it sits inline with text/content like `inline`, but honors box dimensions and all four margins like `block`.

questions.question: How does `display: none` differ from `visibility: hidden`?
options: display: none removes the element from layout entirely (no space reserved); visibility: hidden hides it visually but still reserves its layout space
visibility: hidden also removes the element from the DOM
display: none only works on inline elements
questions.explanation: An element with visibility: hidden still occupies its normal space in the layout, just invisibly; display: none collapses it out of the layout as if it weren't there.
